description: Deterministic, project-authored SAT corpus for trust-cg-sat-host. It mixes a smoke-test tier (50-variable generated random 3-SAT plus tiny PHP) with a benchmark tier (75/100-variable generated random 3-SAT, structured parity, and larger PHP) used by satlib_bench_table to demonstrate JIT amortization, a crafted / application-flavored tier (queens, adder equivalence, blocks-world planning, parity cycle) added to close critical-review limitation #6 of benchmarks/benchmark_study.md ('only random 3-SAT'), and a SAT-Comp-medium tier (php-11-10, 8-bit adder equivalence, three uniform random 3-SAT instances at N=175/200/225) whose native solve dwarfs the JIT compile cost. Eleven filenames beginning with uuf, uf, or aim are retained solely for compatibility with existing tests and benchmark reports; their current contents are generated by generators.py and include no SATLIB or AIM bytes. Total committed bytes stay under 200 KB. The `min_solve_ms_estimate` field (optional) is a rough lower bound on MicroSAT's expected native solve time on a modern x86-64/Apple-Silicon machine; the bench driver flags entries whose measured solve time is far below this as 'too-easy' (and therefore uninteresting for JIT amortization). The `category` field tags each fixture by structural family so the corpus test can print per-category pass counts to stderr.

4-bit ripple-carry adder equivalence miter (UNSAT). Generated by generators.py (adder_equivalence). HWMCC-style structured circuit verification; Tseitin-encoded XOR/AND/OR gates with miter disjunction over output bits.

Blocks-world planning, 3 blocks, 4 time steps (SAT). Generated by generators.py (blocks_world_3_t4). SATPLAN-style encoding (Kautz & Selman 1992) with explicit action preconditions/effects and exactly-one-action-per-step.

Odd-cycle parity UNSAT (33 XOR-2 equations forming a closed odd cycle). Generated by generators.py (parity_unsat). Structured-hard from the Tseitin parity family; long propagation chains with deep learned-clause structure.

Pigeonhole PHP(11,10) constructed programmatically (11 pigeons, 10 holes). Generated by generators.py (pigeonhole). SAT-Comp combinatorial-track-style; exponentially hard for resolution (Haken 1985). MicroSAT solves this in the multi-second range on M-series, well past the ~1.5 ms JIT compile cost, so per-call JIT amortization is observable end-to-end. Empirically: ~13 s native MicroSAT, ~162k propagate calls.

8-bit ripple-carry adder equivalence miter (UNSAT). Generated by generators.py (adder_equivalence). HWMCC-style hardware verification at a larger scale than the 4-bit fixture; Tseitin-encoded XOR/AND/OR gates with miter disjunction over output bits. Mirrors the SAT-Comp HWMCC bounded-equivalence track structurally; identical-circuit miters solve quickly under CDCL because conflict analysis recovers the equivalence relation, so this fixture's value is category coverage, not amortization.

Deterministic uniform random 3-SAT, 175 vars, 750 clauses (ratio 4.29), seed=1. Generated by generators.py (random_3sat_unsat) with the Park-Miller MCG. Extends the generated random tier past N=100 and sits at the SAT/UNSAT phase transition. Empirically: ~2.3 s native MicroSAT, ~62k propagate calls.

Deterministic uniform random 3-SAT, 200 vars, 860 clauses (ratio 4.30), seed=1. Generated by generators.py (random_3sat_unsat). Empirically: ~5.3 s native MicroSAT, ~78k propagate calls. Sits in the middle of the SAT-Comp-medium band.

Deterministic uniform random 3-SAT, 225 vars, 970 clauses (ratio 4.31), seed=1. Generated by generators.py (random_3sat_unsat). Empirically: ~25 s native MicroSAT, ~236k propagate calls. Anchors the upper end of the SAT-Comp-medium band, close to its 30 s release-gate cap.
